summary: In 2026, Agent CI/CD has matured from an emerging practice to a table-stakes requirement. The core shift is that agent behavior is shaped by prompts, model checkpoints, tool definitions, retrieval configs, and guardrails — not just code. This demands eval-driven CI gates, staged pipelines with graduated rollouts, and a closed feedback loop from production traces back into offline datasets.
keyFindings: 89% of production agent teams run observability but only 52% run evals — a 37-point gap where quality silently decays (LangChain State of Agent Engineering Survey, 2026).
Agent-native CI/CD adds 5 gates: golden dataset offline eval, regression blocks, cost gates, shadow eval against production traces, and canary rollout with auto-rollback.
Most teams adopt a 3-tier eval pipeline: (1) deterministic/tool-call tests on every PR, (2) LLM-as-judge regression on nightly schedule, (3) continuous production monitoring with error budgets.
The canonical CI gate pattern: PR triggers eval run against 50-200 golden examples → LLM judge scores outputs → build passes if average score ≥ 0.85 threshold, otherwise PR blocked.
Golden datasets must be version-controlled alongside code, have a named owner, quarterly coverage audits, and a drift detection process.
Tool-call regression suites (recorded cassettes) are the fastest CI tier — sub-second, no API keys, offline replay.

conventionalPipeline.description: Prompt linting, schema validation, ruff/ESLint for deterministic code
Tool-level tests (input validation, output schema, error handling), decoupled from LLM
20-30 tasks against real model, gate on completion rate drop > 5 points
300+ tasks stratified by difficulty/category, gate on p95 latency, cost median, rubric quality
Deploy to staging, shadow 1% replayed production traffic for 1 hour, diff trajectories
5% → 25% → 50% → 100% with automated rollback triggers at every step

threeTierEval.description: Deterministic tool-call tests, simulation stubs/recorded cassettes, no live model. Catches tool selection and argument regressions.
LLM-as-judge scorers across golden dataset. Catches phrasing, reasoning, and semantic regressions.
Sample live traces, score online with lightweight judge, enforce error budgets before promoting canary traffic.

fiveGates: Offline evaluation against curated golden dataset
Regression blocks — per-metric thresholds that block PR if breached
Cost gate — measures token consumption, blocks if >15% increase
Shadow evaluation against replayed production traffic (last 24-72h)

thresholdGuidelines: Regression delta threshold: 0.05 (5 points tolerance for eval noise)
Cost regression gate: block on > 15% token increase per task
hardBlocks: Completion rate drop > 5 points on smoke, > 2 points on full eval
Any guardrail-violation count > 0 on safety-set run
Any unit or contract test failure
softWarnings: Quality rubric mean drop of 0.1-0.2 points
Any tagged category regressed by 3+ points
ciGateStrategies.baselinePolicy: Baseline advances only when a green run on main has non-trivial improvement (completion rate up ≥ 1 point or cost median down ≥ 10%). Never auto-advance on every green run — that causes slow-cooking regressions.

startHere: Latency and token cost per task

evalTypes: Deterministic evals (exact match, schema validation, tool-call regression cassettes) — fastest, sub-second, no API calls
LLM-as-judge evals (G-Eval, rubric-based scoring) — aligns with human judgment 81% of the time
Trajectory evals — score tool selection, parameters, and step order, not just final string
Simulation-based evals — explore new failure modes with no ground truth
Regression evals — committed cassettes block known regressions
evaluationApproach.costConsiderations: 20-test suite × 5 runs with GPT-4o costs $3-8 per PR (~$150-400/month at 50 PRs). Mitigations: run expensive judges only on nightly schedule, use deterministic tests on every commit, restrict LLM-judge to labeled eval/ path changes.

closedLoopFeedback.description: The eval pipeline compounds value when production traces feed back into offline datasets: a failing online scorer automatically promotes offending traces into the offline eval set, so the test suite grows from real user behavior.
closedLoopFeedback.pattern: Offline eval → CI gate → Production trace eval → Error Feed (clusters failing traces) → Dataset expansion → Optimization (agent-opt with Bayesian/Tree-structured/PromptWizard optimizers) → CI
closedLoopFeedback.recommendation: Use the same data layer for production traces and offline eval datasets. When they share a layer, the failing online scorer automatically promotes offending traces into your offline eval set.

maturityModel.level1: Manual eval on release — ad-hoc, skipped under deadline pressure
maturityModel.level2: CI eval gate on every PR — automated golden dataset run, threshold-based blocking
maturityModel.level3: Tiered eval (PR + nightly) — deterministic cheap tests per-commit, LLM-judge on schedule
maturityModel.level4: Production feedback loop — online scoring, trace→dataset promotion, error feed
maturityModel.level5: Continuous optimization — automated prompt/model optimization driven by eval scores, closed-loop improvement
